---
applyTo: "{packages/react/runtime/src/internal.ts,packages/react/runtime/src/snapshot/independent/**,packages/react/runtime/__test__/snapshot/lifecycle/independent*.test.jsx,examples/react/src/transfer-chat.tsx,examples/react/TRANSFER_CHAT.md}"
---

Keep transfer registration, ContextProxy event names, instance generations, props versions and commit ACK queues in `packages/react/runtime/src/snapshot/independent/transfer.ts`, exported as `TransferRegistry` and `transferDiagnostics` from `@lynx-js/react/internal`. ReactLynx owns snapshot root wrappers, first-frame rendering, hydration, patch application, Preact hooks and native event handling. Add only the two renderer factories, `TransferRegistry` and `transferDiagnostics` to the existing `@lynx-js/react/internal` entry. The main-thread renderer provides `initialize`, `createRoot` (returning `render` and `destroy`) and `applyCommit`; the background renderer provides `createRoot` (returning `render`, `hydrate` and `destroy`), `getCurrentRoot`, `flushEvents` and `dispose`. Underlying Snapshot instances, raw patch queues/managers and hook installers remain renderer implementation details. Do not introduce a separate renderer extension entry or install independent renderer hooks on ordinary pages. Use package exports and the application's shared Preact dependency, never relative imports of a second runtime source tree. Run the transfer protocol integration tests in the snapshot runtime harness so both sides exercise the same renderer and native mocks; renderer commit/event hook tests belong under `packages/react/runtime/__test__/snapshot/lifecycle/` and import runtime sources directly. Business code registers component providers and never receives a render context.

Native commands `__CreateTransfer`, `__SetTransferProps` and `__DestroyTransfer` arrive on MTS through `lynx.getNative()` on the Native ContextProxy channel, with the command object directly in event `data`; `__RenderPage` remains an Engine event. MTS/BTS protocol messages use the JS-context/core-context channels. The recorded emulator verification used the earlier Engine command route; the sibling prototype host must migrate its sender to Native before those results can validate the current listeners.
